solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sponges on one endlessly day after day, American feller!

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word that follows is cut off

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday, a day
an axe fells trees, and AX is the American spelling
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
the word day with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: An odd exclamation about a woodcutter from America, out felling day after day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day after day' sounds like repetition; in fact one day is clipped and placed after the other day plus the feller.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaxonida is a zoological order of sponges whose spicules grow along a single axis.

clue.text: Last article dispatched before raising a female tree spirit

definitions.note: the word names both the tree and the spirit distilled from its flowers

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the letters so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dispatched means sent away, so the named article is removed from the word

parts.note: a woman is a female
an is an article, here the one at the end of the word, and it is removed

explanation.surface: A dryad, a female tree spirit, is being banished in some mythical tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female tree spirit' reads as a dryad, but the female is wordplay and the tree spirit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowa is the Indian butter tree, and the same name covers the liquor distilled from its sweet flowers.

clue.text: Revolutionary solarium's offering to put in some opera and swimming facilities

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a solarium offers a tan

indicators.note: put in tells us one short word is placed inside another

parts.note: an aria is one piece of an opera
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sun-bed salon bundling opera tickets with pool access in a promotional deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some opera' is not a hidden word: an aria is part of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Natatoria is the plural of natatorium, an indoor swimming pool or bath.

clue.text: Team quietly welcome, with signs of hesitation, boxer's muscle

parts.note: a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
p, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
hi is a greeting
hum and er are both sounds made while hesitating
Muhammad Ali was the famous boxer, so his is Ali's

explanation.surface: A team greets a boxer with hesitant mumbling as they admire his muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: The xiphihumeralis is a muscle found in some animals running from the breastbone tip to the upper arm bone.

clue.text: Mineral appearing in certain ground

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A geologist notes a mineral found only in particular soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as soil, but here it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacrite is a clay mineral, a kaolin-group silicate of aluminium with a pearly lustre.

clue.text: Manager runs in upset to provoke a little laughter

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards
in places the abbreviation inside the word that follows it

parts.note: to goad is to provoke
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a single ha is a little laughter

explanation.surface: A boss rushes about in a state, getting a few laughs out of the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an emotion, but in a down clue it turns the provoking word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A darogha is an Indian term for a superintendent or overseer, someone in charge of an office or post.

clue.text: Sea vessel getting thus to harbour area

indicators.note: to harbour something is to shelter it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A ship makes its way into a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' looks like the ship's destination; it is the verb that puts A inside SIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A saic is a ketch formerly common in the eastern Mediterranean, a sailing ship of the Levant.

clue.text: A debt collector caught with a crook

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective, fair because 'with a crook' describes something bent like a shepherd's hook

parts.note: taken as written
a dun is one who demands payment of a debt
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bailiff arrested alongside a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' suggests a villain, but here it means a hook or bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Adunc means hooked or curved inwards, so something adunc has a bend like a shepherd's staff.

clue.text: Catch vizier slyly dismissing one royal heir

indicators.note: slyly suggests cunning rearrangement, so the letters are reworked
dismissing sends something away, so that letter is removed first

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, which is removed

explanation.surface: A palace intrigue: trap the scheming chief minister by sidelining the crown prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from CATCH VIZIER and rearrange the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The czarevitch was the eldest son of a Russian tsar and so the heir to the throne.

clue.text: Offend first king in speech about son being a right twister!

definitions.note: adverb in the answer, described here as a manner of being

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: to sin is to offend
first written as 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
R is short for rex, king
orally means by spoken word
s is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An outraged cry about a scandalous royal son who turns out to be a real crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right twister' means one spiralling rightwards, not a dreadful swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinistrorsally describes spiral growth rising from left to right, as some climbing stems and shells coil.

clue.text: Listening device, one about to be replaced with a fibre

indicators.note: replaced with tells us some letters come out and another takes their place

parts.note: a wiretap is a device for listening in on a line
I for one and RE for about, the letters taken out
taken as written, the letter put in

explanation.surface: A bug planted inside some fibre-optic cable.
explanation.walkthrough: IRE in WIRETAP becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Watap is a thread made from the roots of conifers, used by Native Americans for sewing canoes and baskets.

clue.text: Workers, abuzz, gather in this seedy Cairo club

definitions.note: a cryptic description, with workers as worker bees

indicators.note: a seedy place is run down and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Excited staff meet up at a shabby nightclub in Egypt's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are bees and abuzz is literal; seedy also hints at the pollen they collect.
explanation.definitionFit: The corbicula is the pollen basket, a fringed hollow on a worker bee's hind leg where pollen is carried home.

clue.text: Area of pitch out left covered by female magician

parts.note: workers out are on strike, striking

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside, so the letter sits within the name

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned men into swine
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Part of a sports ground lies abandoned, hidden by an enchantress.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside CIRCE. In hockey the striking circle is the D-shaped area in front of goal from which shots must be taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The striking circle is the marked zone on a hockey field inside which an attacker must be to score.

clue.text: Character joining Welsh and UK politicians sharing Mass on odd Sundays

parts.words: Welsh and UK politicians sharing Mass
parts.note: AM, Assembly Member in Wales, and MP, Member of Parliament, overlap on a single M, which stands for Mass

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Cross-party politicians from Cardiff and Westminster attend church together on alternate Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd Sundays' suggests taking alternate letters, but odd is the anagram signal. Wales had Assembly Members, AMs, before its Senedd was renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampussyand is an old dialect name for the ampersand, the symbol standing for 'and', so a character that links words.

clue.text: Increasingly convinced earlier tablet's lacking bite

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: more sure is the comparative of sure
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, and the earlier of the two E's goes

explanation.surface: Someone growing more confident about a pill even though it lacks punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' picks the first of the two E's in MORESURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Morsure is an old word for a bite or biting, from the Latin morsus, a bite.

clue.text: Fuel recycled, since uninitialled order returned

parts.note: as can mean since, because

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read the other way
without an initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a diktat is a harsh decree or order

explanation.surface: Fuel gets recycled because a command came back unsigned.
explanation.walkthrough: A diktat is a decree imposed without consultation; 'uninitialled' plays on an unsigned order losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatki is a liquid fuel made from the residue left over after refining petroleum, waste put to use.

clue.text: Dinosaurs in modern times mostly bound to embrace queen

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter goes
in places the following group inside the shortened word

parts.note: today, the present era, without its last letter

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: to bound is to leap or hop
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Dinosaurs show up these days and must surely surround the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two nested containers: the queen sits inside the bound, which sits inside the clipped modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: Theropoda is the suborder of two-legged, mostly flesh-eating dinosaurs that includes Tyrannosaurus.

clue.text: Nonjurors maybe people getting on with case for unions

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of unions
those who are ageing, getting on in years

explanation.surface: Old people joining up with a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nonjurors were Anglican clergy who refused the oath to William III after 1688; the usagers among them insisted on certain old liturgical usages.
explanation.definitionFit: Usagers were a faction of the Nonjurors who kept particular ritual usages, so a usager is one kind of Nonjuror.

clue.text: Half-inch tip cut from article in secrecy

indicators.note: cutting the tip trims off the end letter of the word

parts.note: half-inch is rhyming slang for pinch, which means steal
the definite article the, with its tip removed

explanation.surface: A carpenter quietly trims half an inch off the end of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-inch' looks like a measurement; in Cockney rhyming slang it rhymes with pinch, to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting secretly or furtively, so as to escape notice.

clue.text: Fashionable binding round middle of area of foot

definitions.note: adjective phrase: relating to a metrical foot

indicators.note: binding means tying around, so the word wraps the letters that follow

parts.note: chic means stylish
a round shape like the letter O

indicators.note: middle of keeps just the central letters of the next word

parts.note: the two central letters of area

explanation.surface: A trendy bandage wrapped round the middle of the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area of foot' wants to be the definition, but area feeds the wordplay and only 'of foot' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Choreic means of a choree, the metrical unit also called a trochee, one long syllable then one short.

clue.text: A number of Poles performing after tea

indicators.note: after places the drink's word first, with the other pieces following it

parts.note: cha or char is British slang for tea
N and S, the north and south poles
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: Several Polish people put on a show once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' means a song here, and 'Poles' are the magnetic poles, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanson is a French song, and a number is a piece of music in a performance.

clue.text: Instrument requiring practice in it by 5th of October — no later

parts.note: it in the sense of sex appeal, SA
usage is customary practice

indicators.note: the fifth of a word means only its fifth letter is used

parts.note: the fifth letter of October
as soon means no later than

explanation.surface: A musician says their instrument needs rehearsal before early October at the latest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice in it' means practice next to it, with SA going first. The sausage bassoon is another name for the racket, a Renaissance double-reed wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sausage bassoon is a nickname for the rackett, a compact Renaissance woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Stop sticking smug nurse's exhibits up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
exhibits means shows, so the letters are on display inside the words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied nurse puts her exhibits on display.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across smug and nurse and are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ungum is to free something from gum, so that it is no longer held fast by adhesive.

clue.text: Two shakes detaching bottom from type of bag

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: a Jiffy bag is a padded envelope

explanation.surface: Shaking a bag twice to get the bottom loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two shakes', as in 'two shakes of a lamb's tail', means a very short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiff is a moment, as is the idiom 'in two shakes', both meaning almost no time at all.

clue.text: Bores, first rate, and without blame, lacking heart, and never ending

indicators.note: lacking a heart means the central letter is removed
never ending means it has no end, so the last letter goes too

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
guiltless means blameless

explanation.surface: A list of virtues describing tedious people as excellent, blameless, heartless and endless.
explanation.walkthrough: GUILTLESS loses its middle T and its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiguilles are rock drills; to bore is to drill a hole, so the boring tools are aiguilles.

clue.text: Eleven in Rome putting forward old philosopher

indicators.note: putting a letter forward changes the order of the word's letters

parts.note: Lazio is a Rome football club, a team of eleven

explanation.surface: A Rome football side promotes an elderly thinker to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven in Rome' tempts towards XI; here it is the Serie A club, whose final O is moved forward two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Laozi is the ancient Chinese sage traditionally credited with founding Taoism.

clue.text: The same, gracious, description of church roof?

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same
my, as in 'my gracious!', an exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming at the same gracious roof of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' sounds like praise for the roof; it is the exclamation 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Domy means dome-like, a fair word for a church roof built as a rounded vault.

clue.text: Fizzy drink readily available after second one's flat?

indicators.note: after sends the abbreviation to the front, with the description following it

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
handy means close at hand
gaff is British slang for one's home

explanation.surface: A sparkling drink is easy to get but goes flat after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests a drink that has lost its fizz; here it is a home, and gaff is British slang for a house or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandygaff is beer mixed with ginger beer or lemonade, a fizzy drink now usually called shandy.
